newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: COST OF DUTCH TRAFFIC JAMS SLIGHTLY UP IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: COST OF DUTCH TRAFFIC JAMS SLIGHTLY UP IN 1996.

text.p: Traffic jams in the Netherlands cost the economy an estimated 1.58 billion guilders in 1996, slightly up from 1.55 billion in the previous year, the Dutch ministry of transport said on Tuesday.
The ministry said the 1996 total corresponded with 63.1 million work hours lost by drivers and passengers by being caught in road congestion. In 1995, some 62.3 million hours were wasted.
The ministry said the number of traffic jams had remained about steady but the average length per congestion had gone up in 1996.
